rule: `valid` is never, by itself, permission to execute. Authorization APIs expose an explicit decision (`authorized`, or a documented equivalent such as `verified`, `official`, `requested_conditions_met`, `claim_verified`).
method: Lexical enumeration by scripts/check-valid-field-decisions.mjs of every `.valid`, `?.valid`, ["valid"], .get("valid") read and `{ valid } =` destructuring in shipped JS/MJS/CJS/HTML/Python, positive valid-only sinks under test/, and every exit-0 / HTTP-2xx decision sink in JS/Python/Go. It does not follow data flow across variables or modules; aliases such as `accepted = result["valid"]` are classified by review (alias_of_valid).

valid_reads.deny-guard: valid=false denies (throw/return/exit non-zero/skip); a true value only lets later checks run.
valid_reads.conjunct: valid is one conjunct of a decision that also requires an explicit decision field or trust input.
valid_reads.signed-verdict-count: a signer verdict counted toward a quorum; permission additionally requires a relying-party-held policy.
valid_reads.report-only: copied into an output, report, log or display; no action is gated on it.
valid_reads.schema-check: type or shape check of a verdict field; malformed input is rejected.
valid_reads.validator-exit: exit status of a validator command whose documented meaning is format/integrity validity only; it executes nothing.
valid_reads.assertion: test or self-check assertion; not an execution path.
